text:
Dougie Hamilton is 33 and playing 21 minutes a night on a Devils team that controls games, and our numbers think he deserves more than ten points in 23 games. He has two goals on 4.2 expected (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and New Jersey has scored about 5.5 fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice. That usually swings back.

He is still a shooter first: 63 shots, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts him in the 94th percentile among defensemen for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net. The surprise is the defense. The same tracking has him stopping 18% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman. He faces tough competition, 97th percentile last season by Evolving-Hockey. With Johnathan Kovacevic out a month, Hamilton's minutes may climb. Our range has him around 38 points.
